result: Any algorithm — even randomized and using all derivatives — needs ε^{−(p+1)/p} queries in the worst case to find an ε-stationary point of a function with Lipschitz p-th derivative; the hard instance is a zero-chain that reveals one coordinate per query. So gradient descent (ε^{−2}) and cubic regularization (ε^{−3/2}) are worst-case optimal.
result_plain: Lower bound ε^-(p+1)/p for finding stationary points; GD and cubic Newton are optimal in their classes.
